title: Publish provider-slot release on the scheduler root
description: Prerequisite for the daemon's atomic attempt/lease/provider-slot release composition. Hard-depend on task-9f51def13fb1484482bcb6d68ce3708d. The pure authority already exists and is QA-approved: `releaseProviderSlot` and `ProviderSlotReleaseCommand` are re-exported by `authority/lease-resource.ts`, but current `@moe/scheduler` root has zero `releaseProviderSlot` export, so a daemon consumer would have to deep-import a package-private module. Publish only this existing transition from the focused scheduler execution surface and ratchet the root namespace. Consumer: the daemon release-state composition task created immediately after this task, then task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4.
definitionOfDone: `@moe/scheduler` publicly exports the existing `releaseProviderSlot` value and `ProviderSlotReleaseCommand` type from their owning module; no duplicate transition or vocabulary is introduced.

The hand-written runtime root roster adds exactly the one new function in reviewed order, updates the explicit count, and pins its defined function binding while retaining exact namespace equality/freeze checks.

The daemon manifest declares `@moe/scheduler`, the lock importer links it, and a temporary compiled probe inside apps/daemon imports and calls `releaseProviderSlot` plus its type from the bare specifier, typechecks exit 0, and is deleted in the same guarded command.
A mutation removing the production root export reddens the named root-roster/probe assertion rather than only a helper; restoring it returns the suite green.
`pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` run separately with a nonzero test-count line and no owned-path regression.
taskRails: Hard-depend on task-9f51def13fb1484482bcb6d68ce3708d; own only its focused scheduler execution-surface TypeScript file and packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts.
Public-surface slice only: do not edit provider-slot-release.ts, lease-resource.ts, daemon composition, package manifests, lockfile, RuntimeCommandKind or schemas.
Use the existing public transition and exact root roster; explicit owned-path commit.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Small two-file publication slice; the only planning decisions were sequencing and where the export lands. (1) Dep task-9f51def1 was WORKING at planning time -- planned with a step-1 verify-or-block rather than blocking outright, because its DoD pins the output shape precisely (a root-reachable execution-surface module forwarded by index.ts, namespace byte-identical, both files <=250 lines) and this task's steps depend only on that shape plus the file's NAME, discoverable at HEAD. This matches the board's verify-or-block convention: the gate covers genuine uncertainty (the split could land differently or be rejected), not certainty performed as a check. (2) The export goes through the NEW surface module, not index.ts -- adding it at the root would recreate the oversized-barrel pattern the split just removed, and the split's whole consumer story ('a later two-file task able to add releaseProviderSlot without editing an oversized source') names this task. (3) DoD 3 vs rail 2 apparent contradiction resolved by measurement: the daemon manifest ALREADY declares @moe/scheduler with a lock importer (verified earlier this session when planning a3e8a02d), so DoD 3 is verification-plus-probe, no manifest edit -- and if the edge were absent the correct move is re-block, because rail 2 forbids touching manifests from this task. (4) The probe CALLS releaseProviderSlot rather than only importing it, per the DoD's own wording -- an import-only probe cannot distinguish a real value export from a type-only leak, the known type-only-export-invisible-to-count-test failure.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at current HEAD plus the dep task's own recorded measurements. SUBJECT: releaseProviderSlot and ProviderSlotReleaseCommand are QA-approved pure authority, re-exported by packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-resource.ts (per this task's description); @moe/scheduler root has ZERO releaseProviderSlot export today, so a daemon consumer would need a deep import into a package-private module -- the exact gap this task closes. SPLIT (task-9f51def1, WORKING): index.ts measured 430 physical lines at HEAD c1ab42b, beyond the split-before-400 cap; its deliverable is a focused execution-surface module holding the authority/resource/budget/fairness export group, index.ts forwarding it, namespace unchanged at the reviewed 94-name set -- so THIS task bumps 94 -> 95 and adds its export to that new module, whose filename must be discovered at HEAD in step 1. OWNERSHIP SPLIT BETWEEN THE TWO TASKS, deliberate: 9f51def1 owns index.ts + the new surface module and may NOT touch index-surface.test.ts; THIS task owns the surface module + index-surface.test.ts and may NOT touch index.ts, provider-slot-release.ts, lease-resource.ts, manifests, or the lockfile. The index-surface suite pins exact namespace equality, an explicit count, and freeze checks over a hand-written roster -- the same set-equality discipline used in apps/daemon's surface suite, and the reason a leaked or missing export cannot pass silently. Daemon edge: apps/daemon/package.json already declares @moe/scheduler with the pnpm-lock importer (verified this session), so the DoD-3 probe needs no manifest work.
planningNotes.risks: Main risk is a file-name race: the owned surface module does not exist until 9f51def1 lands, and its name is that task's choice -- step 1 discovers it rather than guessing, and re-blocks if the split has not landed or was QA-rejected. Second, the two tasks share the surface module file in a shared worktree; if 9f51def1's worker is still mid-QA-fix when this task starts, coordinate rather than colliding -- check `git log -1 -- packages/scheduler/src/<surface>.ts` and the task board before editing. Third, the type-only trap: ProviderSlotReleaseCommand is a type and invisible to runtime roster counts, which is why the probe must CALL the value and the roster must pin the function binding -- a worker who exports the type but fat-fingers the value export would otherwise pass the count. Fourth, the roster must stay hand-written; deriving the expected set from the namespace at runtime would make the equality check a tautology. Fifth, the drill must redden the NAMED member, not just the count -- a count-only failure means the roster assertion enumerates nothing and needs strengthening. Sixth, rail 2's edit bans are wide (no index.ts, no authority modules, no manifests/lockfile): the entire production diff should be a handful of lines in ONE file plus test-roster lines; anything larger is scope creep to reject in self-review. Finally, run the two gate legs separately with their own exit codes -- a `;` chain reports only the last leg and a filtered run with no count line ran nothing.
